uncited: This method enables Multi-Sample Anti-Aliasing (MSAA) rasterization for voxelization without requiring an MSAA render target to be bound to the output merger stage.
*   **Output:** A voxel grid (typically stored in a structured buffer or texture) populated with primitive IDs or coverage data.
*   **Render Target:** A standard, non-MSAA render target (e.g., 1x MSAA) is used.
Create a standard render target view (RTV) for the voxelization output buffer.
Bind the rasterizer state to the pipeline.
Bind the standard (non-MSAA) render target to the Output Merger stage.
Uses primitive expansion to ensure coverage.
More robust against holes but computationally more expensive per primitive. [Link](2480-3-axis-rasterization-voxelization.md)
Optimizes memory access patterns for large voxel grids. [Link](2598-chunked-uv-rasterization-with-face-id-storage.md)
Projects triangles directly into voxel space. [Link](5432-triangle-projection-voxelization.md)
*   **When to use:** When vidmem is constrained and a high-resolution voxel grid can mitigate coverage gaps.
It addresses the memory overhead of traditional MSAA-based voxelization methods.
